title: Overcoming Dynamic I/O Boundaries: a Double-Sided Streaming Methodology with dispel4py and CAPIO
problem: Workflow orchestration systems struggle with strict I/O boundaries that enforce file synchronization barriers between workflow phases, limiting the ability to implement end-to-end streaming across multi-stage applications.
motivation: Eliminating artificial I/O boundaries can enable continuous dataflow processing without phase synchronization delays, improving throughput and reducing memory footprint for large-scale scientific workflows.
method: Introduce a double-sided streaming methodology combining control-plane streaming (dispel4py) with data-plane streaming (CAPIO). Extend CAPIO with a new commit rule for streaming over dynamically generated file sets, enabling hybrid in-memory and file-based dataflows.
key_novelty: Novel commit rule enabling streaming across dynamic file sets without modifying existing workflow logic; seamless integration of control and data-plane streaming without artificial boundaries.
contributions: Double-sided streaming architecture combining control and data planes
Extension to CAPIO supporting streaming over dynamically generated file sets
Elimination of file synchronization barriers in multi-stage workflows
23-40% performance improvement on seismic cross-correlation workload
limitations: Evaluation limited to single seismic workflow; scalability on very large distributed systems not explored.
